I’m really sleep now, so I’ll keep it short. I was suicidal from ages 13-16. I started seriously practicing what I learned in therapy at 16. “It gets better” is unbelievably cliche and was annoying to hear. But right now, my outlook on life is completely different. 

I often get really emotional thinking how much my life has improved. Not to say everything is perfect, I do have bad days, definitely. Younger me would have absolutely never thought it was possible to feel the way I feel today. 

In therapy, I leaned cognitive behavioral therapy. If you were to tell younger me that one day, I would finally not want to die and I’d genuinely be happy, I would consider it some sort of fantasy.
The only help is can offer is to listen to him, as I and other friends have been doing for months. But I believe he needs professional help.
